5. The suit was decreed by the trial court. Being aggrieved thereby the defendant preferred appeal before the District Judge, Nilphamari and the court of appeal below sent the case back on remand for fresh trial on the ground that all the properties of the predecessor of the parties were not brought in the hotchpots of the suit. The suit was again decreed after rehearing. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree of the trial court the defendant preferred Other Appeal No. 22 of 1996. The said appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge, Nilphamari who dismissed the appeal and upheld the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. The defendant then filed Civil Revision No. 4796 of 1998 before the High Court Division and obtained rule. A Single Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing, discharged that rule by the impugned judgment and order dated 1.2.02.2008. 

 6. We have heard Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman the learned Advocate 14 the respondents and gone through the judgments of all the three courts below. It appears that in this suit the main point for determination was whether the unregistered deed of gift dated 11.01.1960 allegedly executed by the original owner Md. Hussain in favour of the defendant No. 1 was genuine or not. Both the courts of facts, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties before the trial court and also examining the alleged signature of Md. Hussain appearing in the said disputed deed of gift dated 11.01.1960 with other admitted signatures of Md. Hussain as per Section 73 of the Evidence Act found that the alleged signature appearing in the said unregistered deed of gift was not of Md. Hussain and as such was not genuine and that the said deed of gift, therefore, was forged. The revisional court appears to have examined the judgments of the courts below and found out that the courts below, on proper and meticulous consideration of the evidence adduced before the trial court, found that the alleged deed, of gift dated 11.01.1960 was not genuine one and that the property was not gilled to the defendant No. 1 by Md. Hussain. The revisional court, on consideration of the evidence on record, did not find any reason to interfere with these concurrent findings of the courts of fact. The revisional court opined that the decisions of the courts below being based on facts, circumstances and evidence on record and there being concurrent findings over points in issue and there being no error of law or fact in passing the judgment the impugned judgment and decree did not warrant any interference by the revisional court.
